Proposed level changes for requirement in chapter "V2 Authentication"

Full list of requirements for the chapter is listed here: https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x11-V2-Authentication.md

| # | Description | Level change |
| :---: | :--- | :---: |
| **1.2.6** | [ADDED, SPLIT FROM 2.2.1] Verify that application documentation defines how controls such as rate limiting, anti-automation, and adaptive response, are used to defend against attacks such as credential stuffing and password brute force. The documentation should make clear how these controls are configured and prevent malicious account lockout. | 1 > 2 |
| **2.1.2** | [MODIFIED] Verify that passwords of at least 64 characters are permitted. | 1 > 2 |
| **2.1.3** | [MODIFIED] Verify that the application verifies the user's password exactly as received from the user, without any modifications such as truncation or case transformation. | 1 > 2 |
| **2.1.5** | [GRAMMAR] Verify that users can change their password. | 1 > 2 |
| **2.1.10** | [MODIFIED, LEVEL L1 > L2] Verify that a user's password stays valid until it is discovered to be compromised or the user rotates it. The application must not require periodic credential rotation. | 2 > 1 |
| **2.2.2** | [MODIFIED] Verify that email is not used as either a single-factor or multi-factor authentication mechanism. | 1 > 3 |
| **2.2.3** | [MODIFIED, SPLIT TO 2.2.10, COVERS 2.5.5] Verify that users are notified after updates to authentication details, such as credential resets or modification of the username or email address. | 1 > 3 |
| **2.2.10** | [ADDED, SPLIT FROM 2.2.3] Verify that users are notified of suspicious authentication attempts. This may include successful or unsuccessful authentication from an unusual location or client, partially successful authentication with only one of multiple factors, successful or unsuccessful authentication after a long period of inactivity or successful authentication after several unsuccessful attempts. | 2 > 3 |
| **2.5.6** | [MODIFIED] Verify that a secure process for resetting a forgotten password is implemented, that does not bypass any enabled multi-factor authentication mechanisms. | 1 > 2 |
| **2.5.7** | [GRAMMAR, LEVEL L2 > L1] Verify that if OTP or other multi-factor authentication factors are lost, that evidence of identity proofing is performed at the same level as during enrollment. | 1 > 2 |
| **2.5.9** | [MODIFIED, MOVED FROM 2.3.3] Verify that renewal instructions for authentication mechanisms which expire are sent with enough time to be carried out before the old authentication mechanism expires, configuring automated reminders if necessary. | 2 > 3 |
| **2.5.10** | [ADDED] Verify that administrative users can initiate the password reset process for the user, but that this does not allow them to change or choose the user's password. This prevents a situation where they know the user's password. | 1 > 3 |
| **2.6.5** | [MODIFIED, MOVED FROM 2.7.2, MERGED FROM 2.8.1] Verify that out-of-band authentication requests, codes, or tokens, as well as time-based, one-time passwords (TOTPs) have a defined lifetime. For out of band this should be 10 minutes and for TOTP this should be as short as possible, usually 30 seconds. | 1 > 2 |
| **2.7.1** | [MODIFIED] Verify that authentication mechanisms using the Public Switched Telephone Network (PSTN) to deliver One-time Passwords (OTPs) via phone or SMS are offered only when alternate stronger methods (such as push notifications) are also offered and when the service provides information on their security risks to users. | 1 > 2 |
| **2.7.3** | [MODIFIED, SPLIT TO 2.6.1] Verify that out-of-band authentication requests, codes, or tokens are only usable for the original authentication request for which they were generated and not a previous or subsequent one. | 1 > 2 |
| **2.11.1** | [ADDED] Verify that, if the application supports multiple identity providers (IdPs), the user's identity cannot be spoofed via another supported identity provider (eg. by using the same user identifier). Usually, the application should register and identify the user using a combination of the IdP ID (serving as a namespace) and the user's ID in the IdP. | 2 > 3 |

previous_versions.body:
> If you integrate an application with an untrusted IdP, you'll have problems anyway.

Doesn't this happens all the time?

It is not supposed to be a problem as long as the users of each IdP are properly segregated (and as long as you don't allow IdPs to grant application-wide authorizations to its users). You trust the "untrusted" IdP to authorize its own user and nothing more (i.e. the different IdPs don't have trust to trust each others). Implemented properly, this is supposed to be fine. This is actually part of the point of 2.11.1.

This is supported through [Self-Issued OpenID Provider](https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html#SelfIssued) and open [OIDC Dynamic client registration](https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-registration-1_0.html#ClientRegistration).
